why: does the design actually live longer, where it lives?

intrinsic_hazard_per_day.source: DESIGN INPUT: an intrinsic hazard of 1/60 per day, a 60-day mean lifespan in protection, taken as the baseline this design is measured against. Stated by the designer; not a survival curve fitted to any data in this repository.

designed_intrinsic_hazard_per_day.source: DESIGN INPUT: the design asks for twice the intrinsic lifespan, 120 days.

extrinsic_hazard_per_day.source: DESIGN INPUT: 0.08 per day, a ~12-day expectation from predation and everything else outside the animal. The ecology layer names 29 taxa recorded as eating this clade and which are recorded in the box asked about; it does NOT give a rate, and this number is the designer turning that list into one.

result.reading: The design changes the INTRINSIC hazard by a factor of 0.5 -- a 2x longer intrinsic lifespan. With the extrinsic hazard at 0.08 /day, expected lifetime goes from 10.345-10.345 days to 11.321-11.321 days: a factor of 1.094 to 1.094. Extrinsic mortality dominates. Abolishing intrinsic mortality ENTIRELY would give 12.5 days, only 1.208x the baseline, so no change to the intrinsic term can buy much here: the animal is not dying of being old.

result.model: Constant two-term hazard, E[T] = 1/(h_intrinsic + h_extrinsic). Exact arithmetic over the declared rates.
result.model_caveat: A CONSTANT hazard makes the lifetime exponential, and real survival curves are not: hazards rise with age, which is what senescence IS, and a Gompertz or Weibull form would capture that. Fitting one needs survival data this repository holds for no organism. So the shape here is assumed, not fitted, and the expectation is a first-order statement that is most wrong exactly where senescence matters most -- at the old end of the curve.
what_this_cannot_say: HOW the design would live longer: no pathway, no gene, no mechanism is represented anywhere in this repository
whether the intrinsic hazard the design claims is achievable at all
what the change costs: life-history theory expects a longer-lived design to pay in fecundity or growth, and nothing here prices that
whether the extrinsic hazard stays put: an organism that lives longer is exposed longer, and may be exposed differently

result.scope: What the design accomplishes, as distinct from its shape or its gait. Three checks, each resting on something that cannot be argued with -- a constant-hazard expectation, Stokes drag, and conservation of mass -- evaluated over quantities the caller declares with sources. It models no mechanism: it does not say HOW the organism would live longer, exert a force or fix carbon, only whether the numbers a designer states are consistent with each other and with physics. A design this layer does not contradict has not been shown to work.
